title: The Orion’s Dilemma: Classic Cinema vs. Live Music

scenario.title: The Orion’s Dilemma: Classic Cinema vs. Live Music
scenario.setting: The chipped red-brick Orion Theater, once a beloved regional spot for 1970s blockbusters and Saturday matinee cartoons, now operates as an intimate live-performance venue in a fading Rust Belt neighborhood. Its former concession stand now sells craft cider and vegan pretzels instead of buttered popcorn, its projection booth repurposed as a soundboard station, and a small group of lifelong residents is fighting to restore its vintage art deco marquee and host monthly classic film screenings alongside the indie folk and punk shows booked by the venue’s young manager.

characters.name: Marv Pritchard
characters.tendencies: He lobbies the city council to block funding for permanent live performance upgrades and organizes monthly classic film screenings in the theater’s side lounge when possible

characters.name: Lila Torres
characters.tendencies: She books local indie acts three nights a week and campaigns to turn the theater’s original balcony into a VIP seating area for ticketed concertgoers

characters.name: Javi Ruiz
characters.tendencies: He helps coordinate hybrid events that pair live music sets with classic film clips to bridge the two sides of the theater’s community debate

characters.name: Gloria Wade
characters.tendencies: She runs a neighborhood newsletter that features both concert listings and classic film event announcements to build unity among the theater’s supporters

turns.name: Marv Pritchard
turns.text:
I’ve been showing up to this theater for classic matinees since I was 10, and I can’t believe the city’s even considering funding permanent live performance upgrades that’d gut the kind of quiet, communal film nights we’ve been running out of the side lounge for two years now. This spot’s legacy isn’t stage lights—it’s big screen blockbusters and Saturday cartoons.
[He adjusts the stack of 16mm film canisters tucked under his arm and smooths a crumpled screening flyer taped crookedly to the concession stand’s side.]

turns.name: Lila Torres
turns.text:
I just confirmed that local indie shoegaze act Soft Signal will play our first VIP balcony showcase next Friday, once we finish patching the drywall in the upper seating area. We already have 42 pre-sold tickets for the spot, which is double what we thought we’d hit in just three days of spreading the word.
[kneeling to brush a layer of dust off the weathered brass plaque marking the theater’s original 1972 balcony entrance, tucked behind the concession stand’s stack of unopened popcorn bags]

turns.name: Javi Ruiz
turns.text:
Good evening, everyone packed into this beloved chipped red-brick Orion Theater—whether you’re a lifelong regular or here for your first hybrid film-music night! We’re kicking things off with a rare 1972 Saturday matinee cartoon clip before the local folk quartet takes the live stage.
[I adjust the height of the projection screen hanging above the stage, running a hand to smooth out a tiny crease in the fabric.]

turns.name: Gloria Wade
turns.text:
Good evening, neighbors popping by the Orion tonight! This month’s community newsletter drops right now, with full listings for our upcoming 1970s retro double features and a roundup of local acts playing the theater’s lobby shows all summer. It’s such a joy to see this old beloved brick spot filled with folks who want to keep its warm spirit alive.
[Brushing a fleck of chipped red brick dust off a stack of freshly printed newsletters before tucking a handful under the concession stand’s front ledge for passersby to grab]

turns.name: Marv Pritchard
turns.text:
Hold up, let’s get our priorities straight first. We’re here to sort out booking the side lounge for next month’s Saturday matinee of *Paper Moon*, not vote on permanent live performance setups that’ll jack up our monthly overhead for years to come. This theater’s legacy is tied to classic Hollywood films, not random indie band showcases.
[Grabs a tattered stack of classic film reservation slips from his canvas bag and slaps them down sharply on the chipped concession counter.]

turns.name: Lila Torres
turns.text:
Good evening, everyone—thanks to the newsletter Gloria just shared, we have official sign-up sheets out by the box office for our first balcony VIP showcase next Friday with Soft Signal. For anyone who’s loved this theater through decades of movies and matinees, this is our chance to save that empty upper level and turn it into a space for intimate live music.
[I lean up to tap the weathered wooden railing of the half-restored balcony overhead, then hold up a stack of bright magenta event flyers to wave at the front rows of the crowd.]

turns.name: Javi Ruiz
turns.text:
Whether you’re a lifelong regular or here for your first hybrid film-music night, thank you all for packing into this chipped Orion tonight. I wanted to share that we wrapped the balcony drywall patches earlier this week, so Soft Signal’s shoegaze VIP showcase is officially locked in for next Friday, paired with a restored 1970s sci-fi favorite.
[Holding up a stack of glossy event fliers while nodding toward Gloria, who was passing out community newsletter sheets by the popcorn machine]

turns.name: Gloria Wade
turns.text:
Good evening, neighbors popping by the Orion tonight! This month’s community newsletter drops right now, with full listings for our upcoming 1970s blockbuster retro series, plus all the details for next Friday’s Soft Signal VIP balcony showcase and volunteer sign-ups to help patch the balcony drywall. Drop a suggestion for your favorite classic film to screen next month in the box by the front door too!
[Holds aloft a stack of glossy black-and-orange newsletters, waving them gently to catch the eye of a group of kids staring up at the vintage Saturday matinee cartoon poster taped to the concession stand wall.]

dm_opening: DM opening: the Marv Pritchard takes a position; the cast gathers around a question the scene has been carrying for a year.
dm_closing: DM closing: the Marv Pritchard still holds the line; the next session's hook — a new member, an old scar — is already at the door.
